comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Reproduced again on 1.9.3-rc.1 against staging: client waited 400ms instead of the 12s Retry-After we injected. Filing as reopened.

content.text: Reproduced again on 1.9.3-rc.1 against staging: client waited 400ms instead of the 12s Retry-After we injected. Filing as reopened.

The official SDK retry middleware treats any 503 as a signal to apply the configured exponential backoff (base 250ms, cap 4s) and ignores the Retry-After header when the server sends a delta-seconds value. Under coordinated maintenance we emit Retry-After: 12, yet the client still hammers /v2/search every few hundred milliseconds.

Spec for the middleware says numeric Retry-After must set the next sleep to at least that many seconds before the usual jitter. Observed sleeps stay under 1s across five consecutive 503s in the integration harness.

Hypothesis: parseRetryAfter only handles HTTP-date form and returns zero for pure integers, after which the backoff branch never substitutes the server hint. Reopened after 1.9.2 claimed a fix — the unit test only covered the HTTP-date branch.
Customers with aggressive concurrency see amplified 503 storms and longer outages when we intentionally shed load.
